original_question: Determine whether travelling-wave solutions exist for the nonlocal aggregation-segregation model with detection kernels from Section 2.3, and if they do, compute or estimate how wave speed depends on kernel shape, perceptual radius, and advection or diffusion parameters.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 49 in §4.5, concerning travelling-wave solutions for the scalar nonlocal problem (2.9) with detection functions chosen from the kernel family in (2.3). ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main mathematical content of the paper's official question: existence of travelling waves, possible computation or estimation of wave speed, and dependence of that speed on kernel shape, perceptual radius, and advection/diffusion rates. It also stays in the nonlocal-perception setting rather than drifting to the delay or boundary-condition problems. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
missing_details: The nearest official target is the scalar equation (2.9), not the explicit cognitive-map system (2.11); calling it only the 'nonlocal aggregation-segregation model' leaves the equation ambiguous between the scalar model (2.9) and the multi-species system (2.10). ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
The paper refers to the kernel forms in equation (2.3) of §2.1 (top-hat, Gaussian, exponential), not to Section 2.3. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, the PDE should be written explicitly: u_t = d Delta u - gamma div(u grad u_{g,R}), where u_{g,R}(x,t) = integral over Omega of u(y,t) g(x-y) dy. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The natural travelling-wave setting in §4.5 is an unbounded domain, and the paper writes travelling waves in the form u(x,t) = w(x-ct); this should be stated explicitly. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The parameters should be named explicitly: diffusion rate d, advection strength gamma, perceptual radius R >= 0, and the choice of detection kernel g from (2.3); the sign of gamma determines attraction versus repulsion. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

No algebraic ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency condition, or 'for all sufficiently large m' quantifier is relevant here; the omitted structure is PDE-specific: domain, kernel class, convolution operator, and travelling-wave ansatz. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
refined_question: For the scalar nonlocal aggregation/segregation equation (2.9) on the natural unbounded one-dimensional travelling-wave domain Omega = R, namely u_t = d u_xx - gamma d/dx(u d/dx u_{g,R}) with u_{g,R}(x,t) = integral over R of u(y,t) g(x-y) dy and g chosen as one of the perceptual kernels in (2.3) (top-hat, Gaussian, or exponential, with perceptual radius R >= 0), do there exist travelling-wave solutions u(x,t) = w(x-ct)? If so, can the wave speed c be computed or estimated as a function of the detection kernel g, the perceptual radius R, and the advection and diffusion rates gamma and d? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
justification: The draft is closest to Open Problem 49, not Open Problem 53. The paper reserves the label 'aggregation/segregation models' for (2.9)-(2.10), and Open Problem 49 is the scalar travelling-wave question whose wording matches the draft almost item-for-item: kernel choice from (2.3), perceptual radius, and advection/diffusion dependence. Open Problem 53 instead concerns the different system (2.11) with an additional cognitive-map equation and asks further about extension to n interacting species, which the draft does not mention. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
